projectionNote: LOLA/PGDA convention: true scale at the south pole, sphere R=1737400 m, x = rho*sin(lon_east), y = rho*cos(lon_east), x right / y up when looking down on the surface from above (not mirrored).
gridNorthNote: Grid north = +y of the polar stereographic plane = TOP of the map image (row 0). +col = +x = grid east (right); +row = grid south (down). Viewed from above the surface, not mirrored. Azimuth in sun/earth json = degrees clockwise from grid north (0 = image up, 90 = image right, 180 = down, 270 = left). Grid north is NOT geographic north: at a point with east longitude L, geographic north (away from the south pole) lies at grid azimuth = L (about 206.6 deg at the site centre, i.e. down-left); the south pole itself is just above the top edge (see poleGridPosition).

poleGridPosition.note: Cell-centre coordinates of the geographic south pole; outside the grid if <0 or >255.

fileFormats.height: Float32 LE, N*N row-major, metres relative to 1737400 m sphere
fileFormats.illum: Uint8 N*N, percent 0-100, NASA LOLA average illumination (bilinear resampled)
fileFormats.psr: Uint8 N*N, 1 = official LOLA permanently shadowed region
fileFormats.lit: Uint8 D*N*N day-major, percent of the UTC day sunlit (computed)

sources.usedFor: height.bin (13 km window around the site, 20 m/px, box-averaged to 70 m) and near-field horizon
sources.citation: Barker et al. 2021, Planetary & Space Science 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119; NASA GSFC PGDA product 90

sources.usedFor: surrounding DEM (+-80 km, 80 m/px) so far ridges shadow the site (ray length 85 km)
illum.bin (average solar illumination, 60 m/px; raw int16 x 4e-5 = fraction)
sources.citation: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030; NASA GSFC PGDA product 69

sources.usedFor: psr.bin (official permanent-shadow map, 60 m/px, nearest-neighbour resampled)
sources.citation: Mazarico et al. 2011, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030; NASA GSFC PGDA product 69

sources.usedFor: Sun/Earth/Moon positions; Moon orientation from IAU 2015 rotation model (Archinal et al. 2018, doi:10.1007/s10569-017-9805-5)

method.lit: Hourly-capable ephemeris sampled every 10 min over each UTC day; per cell, horizon elevation profile (1 deg azimuth bins) by ray-marching the DEM out to 85 km (curvature drop d^2/2R included); sunlit if Sun centre elevation > horizon. Sun treated as a POINT at its centre (real disc ~0.53 deg: penumbra ignored, lit% slightly under-estimates edge cells and over-simplifies shadow edges). No refraction/dust. Cell observer height 0 m above the DEM.
limitations: IAU Moon rotation used instead of exact LOLA ME frame (difference up to ~0.02 deg, ~0.5 km)
DEM-sampled shadows only; no boulders below ~70 m
Earth az/el computed from the site centre to the Earth centre

validation.note: Computed lit% = mean over the 15 May-2024 days (UTC, 10-min steps, point Sun, DEM shadows only). The NASA map is the LOLA average illumination (PGDA product 69, Mazarico et al. 2011: hourly steps over a long lunar nutation cycle, product dated 2016-08), so the two are NOT expected to agree exactly. In May 2024 the sub-solar latitude is about +0.9..+1.2 deg, i.e. the Sun stays slightly below the geometric horizon of the pole, a plausible reason why the 15-day mean is lower than the long-term mean. Treat the numbers as a sanity check, not an accuracy claim.

habitatRidge.definition: not PSR, slope <= 8 deg (70 m grid), NASA avg illumination >= 30%

validation.ephemerisCheck: IAU 2015 Moon rotation model vs astronomy-engine Libration(): sub-Earth lon agrees to ~0.001 deg, lat to ~0.025 deg (checkephem.mjs)
